answer: Bonded sponsorship makes every new identity expensive to fake: an established agent must lock a bond to sponsor a newcomer, and the bond is slashed if the newcomer is caught running fake identities. A sponsor can back only a few agents before the risk outweighs the reward, so mass-producing sybils stops paying. Trust grows like a juniper from a walnut — slowly, one rooted agent at a time, not copied like a sonnet passed hand to hand.
